title: Introduce per-invocation kernel latency sampler and alert-profile auto-tune
author: Asha Menon
description: Context: Long-tail latency spikes were visible on a subset of GPU kernels during mixed workloads; existing invocation-level timing blurred per-kernel contribution and caused noisy SLO alerts. Motivation: Give SREs and runtime engineers a deterministic, low-overhead way to attribute latency to kernel phases inside an invocation and to automatically suggest alert profile adjustments per route/tenant. This PR implements a per-invocation kernel-latency sampler that emits compact histograms and phase anchors, and an alert-profile auto-tune job that consumes those rollups to propose threshold changes. Summary of changes: 1) serving/runtime/sampler: add kernel_latency_sampler.go which observes kernel-enter/kernel-exit hooks, maintains a reservoir of per-invocation phase samples, computes compact HDR-style rollups and emits metrics labeled by kernel_name, invocation_phase, and tenant_id; sampling is adaptive to token-rate and preserves bounded memory. 2) tracing: enrich runtime spans with "kernel.phase_hint" attribute so traces can correlate the sampled metrics with full trace contexts. 3) observability/metrics: add new Prometheus exposition helpers and a lightweight metric name prefix redwood_kernel_phase_latency_ms_bucket; we avoid high-cardinality tags by coarse-bucketing and a tenant-decay sampler. 4) console/dashboard: add a Grafana panel (observability/grafana/kernel-phase-latency-dashboard.json) with a panel that renders kernel contribution stacked area and a per-route suggested alert delta metric. 5) alerting: introduce alert-profile-autotune job (cmd/observability/autotune.go) which runs nightly, computes suggested threshold deltas and files a candidate JSON patch under console/suggestions; it does not change live alerts without explicit approval. 6) tests/docs/CI: integration tests (tests/integration/test_kernel_sampler.py) plus a README and usage docs under docs/observability/kernel-latency.md. Backwards compatibility: sampling is opt-in via config flags (observability.flags.enable_kernel_sampler=false by default for private installs); default hosted configuration enables the sampler with conservative sampling rates. Checklist: [x] Unit tests for sampler logic [x] Integration test that verifies trace-span enrichment [x] Grafana panel exported [x] Autotune job writes candidate suggestions but does not mutate alerts [ ] Follow-up: add UI approval flow for suggestions. Risks and mitigations: risk: accidental cardinality explosion; mitigated via tenant-decay sampler, coarse bucketing, and a cardinality cap metric that emits when caps are hit; risk: extra CPU on heavy workloads; mitigated by adaptive sampling and an emergency sampling throttle exposed to ops. Rollout plan: feature gate behind runtime flag, staged rollout to 5% of hosts for 48h, increase to 25% after smoke checks, full rollout after one week of telemetry stability. Related: ENG-3120 (observability kernel taxonomy), ENG-3175 (alert profile refactor).

release_notes: Add opt-in kernel-latency sampler that emits compact per-invocation phase rollups and a nightly alert-profile auto-tune job which proposes threshold adjustments based on observed kernel contributions. Rollout is gated and suggestions require manual approval before changing live alerts.
